title: Dry Peanut Chutney
name: Dry Peanut Chutney (Shengdana Pudi)
subtitle: A ground peanut condiment with chana dal and sesame — mild enough for the whole family.
protein: ~3g protein per 2 tbsp serving — from peanuts, chana dal and sesame

method.title: Roast peanuts and sesame
items: Roast {@peanuts} in the Ninja Crispi in batches of {=1½ cups}, in a single layer so they roast instead of steaming
Set to 330°F for 6 min — the Crispi's lowest setting; shake the basket at 3 min
Check at 5 min: they should be fragrant with crackled skins; add 1 min at a time only
Cool completely on a plate, at least 15 min; rub between your palms to loosen the skins and blow them away
Dry roast {@sesame} in a pan on low flame, stirring constantly 60–90 sec; they pop, so keep a lid nearby
Take them off the moment they turn lightly golden and toasty; cool on a separate plate

method.title: Temper the spices
items: Heat {@oil} in a small pan on medium-low
Fry {@curry-leaves} 20–30 sec until crisp; remove and set aside
In the same oil on low, roast {@chilies} and {@cumin} 60–90 sec until the cumin is golden; do not let them blacken
Return {@curry-leaves|the curry leaves}, then move everything to a plate and cool completely

method.title: Grind: spice base first, then peanuts
items: Add the cooled spice mixture to a grinder with {@chana-dal}, {@sesame|the roasted sesame}, {@hing}, {@salt} and {@amchur}
Grind to a fine powder, 25–35 sec; the dal and seeds must be fine now, not pulsed later
Add {@peanuts|the roasted, cooled peanuts}
Pulse only, 3–4 bursts of 2–3 sec, until coarse and sandy, not a paste
Taste and adjust the seasoning

method.label: Toddler — usage note (powder contains Kashmiri chili)
items: The chili here gives colour more than heat, but keep her serving to ½ tsp maximum
Mix with a few drops of ghee into warm dal-rice or yogurt rice, or sprinkle on a soft ghee roti
For adult heat, add chili flakes at serving instead of into the jar

method.title: Cool and store
items: Spread the powder on a wide plate and rest it uncovered 20 min to drive off any residual moisture
Pack into a clean, dry, airtight glass jar and label with the date
Keep 3–4 weeks at room temperature, or 6–8 weeks refrigerated
Always use a dry spoon; a single drop of moisture shortens shelf life fast

method.label: Tip
method.text: Grind the spice base fine before the peanuts go in, then only pulse; peanut oil releases fast and a few extra seconds makes peanut butter. If the finished powder tastes flat without tamarind → add a squeeze of lemon to the rice at serving, never into the jar.
